phase1_operator_rulings.R6_rerender_selection: PRESERVE the selection if the region still exists, else fall back to the first. No input document stated a policy. Requires TWO acceptance arms: a lone 'preserved' arm is green on an implementation that never re-selects, and a lone 'fallback' arm is green on one that always resets - neither alone distinguishes the spec from its two failure modes. Interacts with HLR-116: focus must follow selection or the keyboard story silently regresses. FOLDED: HLR-116, split into AT-B77-13 (preserve) and AT-B77-14 (fallback) per C-18, plus LLR-116.4/116.5.
phase1_operator_rulings.R7_overflow: WIDEN THE BAR FIRST, THEN AGGREGATE. (1) Rebalance the layout: the bar gets only 21 of the 52 columns #map_grid has at 120x30 - give it a larger share via CSS, MEASURING both axes and the whole pane budget first (C-23/C-29), since a weight that fits the bar can starve a sibling off-screen. (2) Where it still overflows, merge the SMALLEST ADJACENT runs into one aggregate segment with a '+N more' disclosure, following R-TUI-098's precedent of naming only items that actually lost content. HLR-111 also needs a NORMATIVE ALLOCATION BOUND over n_runs + n_gaps vs measured width - an output-shaped predicate cannot bound an allocation (batch-74).
phase1_operator_rulings.R8_stats_fold: ACCEPT the deepened scroll and register it as a carry (C-77-k). The widened bar is what makes regions visible - the batch's purpose - and the stats line is ALREADY below the fold at both regimes today, so this deepens an existing scroll rather than newly hiding anything (31->33 at 120x30). Narrowing the widen to protect it was REJECTED: every column surrendered lowers the ceiling on visible regions.
phase1_operator_rulings.R9_disclosure_surface: Render '+N more' in the REGION LIST, not the bar. Bar columns are the scarce resource the design is contending for, and the list is already the textual per-region surface. B3 holds - the row carries a COUNT, never file-derived text.
